reading: Art crime investigators and security experts say burglaries from galleries across Europe are becoming more brazen.
When thieves broke into a French museum earlier this week and stole four paintings by the impressionist artist Pierre-Auguste Renoir, worth millions of euros, not everyone was surprised.
Just last month, the European policing agency (Europol) had warned that museum thefts across Europe were growing increasingly brazen.
Internationally known art detective Arthur Brand predicted to the BBC that more high-profile burglaries were likely, particularly after the successful robbery at the Louvre in Paris last October.
The audacious crime in one of the world's most famous museums stunned France, and the stolen jewellery worth €88m (£75m) has still not been recovered, nearly a year on.
Brand believes that the Louvre's successful breach signalled to thieves globally that local museums with valuable items might also be targeted.
Europol indicates that the number of reported museum theft cases across Europe began to increase approximately two years ago.
Its recent report says both the methods and targets of thefts are changing, with a rise in more forceful tactics and a focus on high-value items such as precious metals and gemstones.

The Association for Research into Crimes against Art (ARCA) says the recent thefts show a repeated preference for small, portable, immediately accessible objects and for attacks designed to be completed in minutes.
These crimes threaten what many consider invaluable artefacts of historical and cultural value enjoyed by the public.
Brand argues that museums are inherently vulnerable compared with well-secured jewellery shops and banks.
Directors historically 'never have enough money for security' or prefer to spend it on the next exhibition, and museums are often housed in old buildings that are difficult to protect.
Museums are also open public spaces that have less access control, allowing perpetrators to come in as visitors.
Many of these burglaries are over in minutes and the thieves have long gone by the time police show up; the Renoir case happened within five minutes.
Heists used to depend on deception, but burglaries are now becoming increasingly violent, with offenders using tools such as sledgehammers, axes, crowbars, and even explosives.
Precious metals can be easily melted down, leaving no trace for law enforcement, and facilitating illicit sales during the fencing process.

Experts say the trick is to create physical barriers that will delay thieves so there is time for the police to arrive, or to make any theft take so long that it would deter would-be offenders from attempting it.
Security is about buying time, making removal difficult, noisy, detectable and, above all, time-consuming, because thefts can always happen.
Sokka says it's critical to have integrated systems, so for example, if an alarm goes off, you could shut down the facility or lock down all high net worth paintings.
Mayor Caviezel says finding the money for security measures is 'one of our main challenges' for a small city entrusted with national collections.
It could also involve training guards to spot suspicious people who may be casing a museum, which may deter them from returning.
Ultimately, a museum cannot be a fortress; it must balance openness with new standards for facing challenges and attacks.

vocabulary.definition: attracting a lot of public attention and interest; prominent.
an act of breaking or failing to observe a law, agreement, or code of conduct; or a gap in a wall, barrier, or defense, often referring to a security system.
points out, shows, or suggests something, often providing a sign or evidence.
characterized by strength, power, or strong influence; effective or vigorous.
extremely useful, precious, or valuable; beyond estimation in value.
in a permanent, essential, or characteristic way; by its very nature.
individuals who commit a crime or carry out a harmful, illegal, or immoral act.
the act of hiding the truth or misleading someone, especially to gain an advantage.
the illegal practice of receiving, concealing, or selling stolen goods.
to observe and study a place or person, often repeatedly or discreetly, in preparation for a crime or robbery.

entries.ja: 多くの人々の注目と関心を集めること。際立った。
entries.ko: 많은 대중의 관심과 흥미를 끄는; 두드러지는.
entries.zh-Hans: 吸引大量公众关注和兴趣的；显赫的。
entries.es: Que atrae mucha atención e interés del público; prominente.
entries.pt-BR: Que atrai muita atenção e interesse do público; proeminente.

entries.ja: 法律、合意、または行動規範を破る行為。また、壁、障壁、防御における隙間や穴で、しばしばセキュリティシステムについて使われる。
entries.ko: 법률, 합의 또는 행동 규범을 위반하거나 지키지 않는 행위; 또는 벽, 장벽, 방어선에 생긴 틈이나 구멍으로, 종종 보안 시스템을 가리킬 때 쓰인다.
entries.zh-Hans: 违反或未能遵守法律、协议或行为准则的行为；或者墙壁、障碍物或防御系统中的缺口，常指安全系统方面的漏洞。
entries.es: Un acto de romper o no cumplir una ley, acuerdo o código de conducta; o una brecha o apertura en una pared, barrera o defensa, a menudo refiriéndose a un sistema de seguridad.
entries.pt-BR: Um ato de quebrar ou não observar uma lei, acordo ou código de conduta; ou uma abertura em uma parede, barreira ou defesa, frequentemente se referindo a um sistema de segurança.

entries.ja: 何かを指摘する、示す、または示唆すること。しばしば兆候や証拠を提供する。
entries.ko: 어떤 것을 지적하거나 보여주거나 암시하며, 종종 징후나 증거를 제공하는 것을 말한다.
entries.zh-Hans: 指出、显示或暗示某事，通常提供迹象或证据。
entries.es: Señalar, mostrar o sugerir algo, a menudo proporcionando una señal o evidencia.
entries.pt-BR: Aponta, mostra ou sugere algo, frequentemente fornecendo um sinal ou evidência.

entries.ja: 力、権力、または強い影響力によって特徴づけられること。効果的または精力的な。
entries.ko: 힘, 권력 또는 강력한 영향력으로 특징지어지는; 효과적이거나 활기찬.
entries.zh-Hans: 以力量、权力或强大影响力为特征的；有效的或充满活力的。
entries.es: Caracterizado por la fuerza, el poder o una gran influencia; eficaz o enérgico.
entries.pt-BR: Caracterizado por força, poder ou forte influência; eficaz ou vigoroso.

entries.ja: 非常に役に立つ、貴重な、または価値のあること。価値を計り知れないほど。
entries.ko: 극도로 유용하거나 귀중하며, 그 가치를 헤아릴 수 없을 정도로 소중한.
entries.zh-Hans: 极其有用、珍贵或有价值的；价值无法估量的。
entries.es: Extremadamente útil, precioso o valioso; de valor inestimable.
entries.pt-BR: Extremamente útil, precioso ou valioso; de valor inestimável.

entries.ja: 永久的な、本質的な、または特徴的な方法で。その性質上。
entries.ko: 영구적으로, 본질적으로 또는 특징적으로; 그 본성상.
entries.zh-Hans: 以一种永久的、本质的或特有的方式；就其本质而言。
entries.es: De una manera permanente, esencial o característica; por su propia naturaleza.
entries.pt-BR: De maneira permanente, essencial ou característica; por sua própria natureza.

entries.ja: 犯罪を犯したり、有害、違法、または不道徳な行為を実行したりする人々。
entries.ko: 범죄를 저지르거나 해롭고 불법적이거나 부도덕한 행위를 실행하는 개인들.
entries.zh-Hans: 实施犯罪或进行有害、非法或不道德行为的个人。
entries.es: Individuos que cometen un crimen o llevan a cabo un acto dañino, ilegal o immoral.
entries.pt-BR: Indivíduos que cometem um crime ou realizam um ato prejudicial, ilegal ou imoral.

entries.ja: 真実を隠したり、特に優位を得るために誰かを誤解させたりする行為。
entries.ko: 진실을 숨기거나 누군가를 오도하는 행위로, 특히 이점을 얻기 위해 행해진다.
entries.zh-Hans: 隐藏真相或误导某人，特别是为了获得优势的行为。
entries.es: El acto de ocultar la verdad o engañar a alguien, especialmente para obtener una ventaja.
entries.pt-BR: O ato de esconder a verdade ou enganar alguém, especialmente para obter uma vantagem.

entries.ja: 盗品を受け取ったり、隠したり、販売したりする違法な行為。
entries.ko: 도난당한 물품을 받거나 숨기거나 판매하는 불법적인 관행.
entries.zh-Hans: 非法接收、隐藏或销售赃物的行为。
entries.es: La práctica ilegal de recibir, ocultar o vender bienes robados.
entries.pt-BR: A prática ilegal de receber, ocultar ou vender bens roubados.

entries.ja: 犯罪や強盗の準備として、場所や人物を繰り返し、または密かに観察し研究すること。
entries.ko: 범죄나 강도를 준비하기 위해 한 장소나 사람을 반복적으로 또는 은밀하게 관찰하고 연구하는 것.
entries.zh-Hans: 为了犯罪或抢劫做准备，反复或秘密地观察和研究某个地方或人物。
entries.es: Observar y estudiar un lugar o persona, a menudo repetidamente o discretamente, en preparación para un crimen o robo.
entries.pt-BR: Observar e estudar um lugar ou pessoa, frequentemente de forma repetida ou discreta, em preparação para um crime ou roubo.
